questions.question:
The respective ratios between the numerical values of a curved surface area and the volume of a right circular cylinder is 1 : 7. If the respective ratio between the diameter and height of the cylinder is 7 : 6, what is the total surface area of the cylinder?

 {Use } pi = (22)/(7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of CSA to Volume = (2πrh) ÷ (πr²h) = 2/r = 1/7 ⇒ r = 14 unit

Ratio of diameter to height = 2r/h = 7/6

⇒ (2 × 14)/h = 7/6 ⇒ h = 24 unit

TSA = 2πr(r + h) = 2 × (22/7) × 14 × (14 + 24)

⇒ TSA = 88 × 38 = 3344 unit²

**∴ The correct answer is 3344 unit².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 

 
 

 
•

• 
 
• 
 
• 
 h = 24
 TSA = 3344 unit²

**Given:**

Ratio of curved surface area to volume = 1 : 7

Ratio of diameter to height = 7 : 6

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of cylinder = 2πrh

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

Total Surface Area (TSA) of cylinder = 2πr(r + h)

Where r is the radius and h is the height.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Ratio of CSA to Volume = (2πrh) ÷ (πr²h) = 2 / r

⇒ According to the question, 2 / r = 1 / 7

⇒ r = 14 unit

⇒ Diameter (d) = 2r = 2 × 14 = 28 unit

⇒ Given ratio of diameter to height (d / h) = 7 / 6

⇒ 28 / h = 7 / 6

⇒ h = (28 × 6) ÷ 7 = 24 unit

⇒ TSA = 2πr(r + h)

⇒ TSA = 2 × (22/7) × 14 × (14 + 24)

⇒ TSA = 2 × 22 × 2 × 38

⇒ TSA = 88 × 38 = 3344 unit²

**∴ The correct answer is 3344 unit².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cone Properties

A right circular cone with radius r and height h has Volume = (1/3)πr²h and Curved Surface Area = πrl, where slant height l = √(r² + h²).

Sphere Properties

For a solid sphere of radius r, Volume = (4/3)πr³ and Total Surface Area = 4πr².

Hemisphere Properties

For a solid hemisphere of radius r, Volume = (2/3)πr³, Curved Surface Area = 2πr², and Total Surface Area = 3πr².
</p

questions.question: If 8 years ago from now, a grandmother's age was 13 times the age of her granddaughter and after 12 years from now, the grandmother's age will be 3 times her granddaughter's age, then what is the difference of their ages at present (in years)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio 8 years ago = 13 : 1 (Difference = 12 units)

Ratio 12 years later = 3 : 1 (Difference = 2 units)

Since the age difference is always constant, multiply the second ratio by 6 → 18 : 6 (Difference = 12 units)

Change in ratio = 18 − 13 = 5 units, which corresponds to 20 years (8 years past + 12 years future).

1 unit = 20 ÷ 5 = 4 years, so the constant age difference of 12 units = 12 × 4 = 48 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 48 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

8 years ago, Grandmother's age was 13 times the Granddaughter's age.

After 12 years, Grandmother's age will be 3 times the Granddaughter's age.

**Formula Used:**

Present Age = Past Age + Time Passed

**Calculations:**

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 8 Years Ago
 Present
 12 Yrs After
 
 Grandmother
 Granddaughter
 
 
 13x

 13x+20
 
 
 x+20

 After 12 Yrs Ratio = 3 : 1

Let Granddaughter's age 8 years ago be x.

⇒ Grandmother's age 8 years ago = 13x

Total time elapsed from 8 years ago to 12 years after present = 8 + 12 = 20 years.

⇒ Grandmother's age after 12 years = 13x + 20

⇒ Granddaughter's age after 12 years = x + 20

According to the given condition:

⇒ 13x + 20 = 3 × (x + 20)

⇒ 13x + 20 = 3x + 60

⇒ 10x = 40

⇒ x = 4

The difference in their ages is a constant value at any point in time.

⇒ Age difference = 13x − x = 12x

⇒ Age difference = 12 × 4 = 48

**∴ The correct answer is 48 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of any two individuals remains absolutely constant throughout their lives regardless of the time passed.

Ratio Equalization Method

When the same number of years is added to two ages, their difference in ratio parts must be equal. Multiply the ratios by each other's difference to balance them perfectly without relying on algebraic equations.

Reference Age Variable

Whenever solving age problems, it is usually simpler to assign 'x' to the youngest person's age at the earliest mentioned point in time (past) to strictly avoid complex subtractions and fractions.
</p

questions.question: The value of 16³ - 10³ is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Memorizing cubes up to 20 helps in solving directly without complex multiplication.

Cube of 16 = 16³ = 4096

Cube of 10 = 10³ = 1000

Required Difference = 4096 − 1000 = 3096

**∴ The correct answer is 3096.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 16³ − 10³

**Formula Used:**

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Here, a = 16 and b = 10

⇒ 16³ − 10³ = (16 − 10)(16² + 16 × 10 + 10²)

⇒ 16³ − 10³ = 6 × (256 + 160 + 100)

⇒ 16³ − 10³ = 6 × 516

⇒ 16³ − 10³ = 3096

**∴ The correct answer is 3096.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Cubes Identity

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)

Cube of a Binomial (Addition)

(a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)

Cube of a Binomial (Subtraction)

(a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b)
</p

questions.question: {If } 43 times 43 = 1849, { then } 4.3 times 4.3 { equals to:}
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In decimal multiplication, the total number of decimal places in the product is the sum of the decimal places in the multipliers.

Here, the number 4.3 has 1 decimal place.

So, 4.3 × 4.3 will have 1 + 1 = 2 decimal places in total.

We are given that 43 × 43 = 1849.

Placing the decimal point 2 places from the right gives 18.49.

**∴ The correct answer is 18.49.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

43 × 43 = 1849

**Calculation:**

⇒ We need to find the exact value of 4.3 × 4.3

⇒ First, express the decimal numbers as fractions:

⇒ 4.3 = 43 ÷ 10

⇒ 4.3 × 4.3 = (43 ÷ 10) × (43 ÷ 10)

⇒ 4.3 × 4.3 = (43 × 43) ÷ (10 × 10)

⇒ Substitute the given value of 43 × 43 = 1849

⇒ 4.3 × 4.3 = 1849 ÷ 100

⇒ 4.3 × 4.3 = 18.49

**∴ The correct answer is 18.49.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Multiplying Decimals Rule

Multiply the numbers as if they were whole numbers ignoring the decimals. Then, count the total number of decimal digits in the question and place the decimal point so the product has the exact same total number of decimal places.

Dividing by Powers of 10

To divide any number by 10, 100, 1000, etc., shift the decimal point to the left by the exact number of zeros present in the denominator.

Squares Ending in 3

The square of any number that ends with the digit 3 will always have 9 as its unit digit. For example, 3² = 9, 13² = 169, 23² = 529, and 43² = 1849.
</p

questions.question: The distance between points A and B is 966 km. Kamlesh travels from A to B at a speed of 52 km/hr and returns at a speed of 118 km/hr. Calculate Kamlesh’s average speed for the entire journey (round off the answer to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the distance covered in both directions is exactly the same, the average speed can be calculated directly without using the distance value.

Average Speed = (2 × S₁ × S₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

Average Speed = (2 × 52 × 118) ÷ (52 + 118)

Average Speed = 12272 ÷ 170 ≈ 72.188 km/hr

Rounding off to two decimal places gives 72.19 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 72.19 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between A and B = 966 km

Speed from A to B (S₁) = 52 km/hr

Speed from B to A (S₂) = 118 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 
 
 A
 
 B
 
 
 
• 
 
 
 

 

 52 km/hr
 Distance = 966 km

 
 

 

 118 km/hr
 Distance = 966 km
 
 
 Average Speed = ?

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 966 + 966 = 1932 km

⇒ Total Time = (966 ÷ 52) + (966 ÷ 118)

⇒ Total Time = 966 × [(1 ÷ 52) + (1 ÷ 118)]

⇒ Total Time = 966 × [(118 + 52) ÷ (52 × 118)]

⇒ Total Time = 966 × [170 ÷ 6136]

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

⇒ Average Speed = 1932 ÷ (966 × 170 ÷ 6136)

⇒ Average Speed = (1932 × 6136) ÷ (966 × 170)

⇒ Average Speed = (2 × 6136) ÷ 170

⇒ Average Speed = 12272 ÷ 170 = 72.188... km/hr

⇒ Rounding off to two decimal places, we get 72.19 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 72.19 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Unequal Distances

When a person travels different distances at different speeds, Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Average Speed for Three Equal Distances

If a person covers three equal distances at speeds x, y, and z, Average Speed = (3 × x × y × z) ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Relative Speed

When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂. When moving in the same direction, Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|.
</p

questions.question: P and Q together can fill a cistern with water in 12 hours. If P alone can fill the cistern with water in 18 hours, then in how many hours will Q alone fill one-fourth of the same cistern with water?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity of the cistern = LCM(12, 18) = 36 units.

Combined efficiency of P and Q = 36 ÷ 12 = 3 units/hour.

Efficiency of P alone = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 units/hour.

Efficiency of Q alone = 3 − 2 = 1 unit/hour.

Time taken by Q to fill 1/4th of the cistern = (36 × 1/4) ÷ 1 = 9 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P and Q together to fill the cistern = 12 hours

Time taken by P alone to fill the cistern = 18 hours

**Method Used:**

We use the LCM method to find the total capacity of the cistern and individual efficiencies of the pipes.

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Hours**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 P + Q
 12
 36
 36 ÷ 12 = 3
 
 

 P
 18
 36 ÷ 18 = 2
 
 

⇒ Efficiency of Q = Combined Efficiency of (P + Q) − Efficiency of P

⇒ Efficiency of Q = 3 − 2 = 1 unit/hour

⇒ Total capacity of the cistern = 36 units

⇒ One-fourth of the cistern's capacity = 36 × (1/4) = 9 units

⇒ Time taken by Q alone to fill 1/4th of the cistern = Work to be done ÷ Efficiency of Q

⇒ Time taken by Q = 9 ÷ 1 = 9 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 9 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Work Formula

If pipe A fills a tank in x hours and pipe B fills it in y hours, the time taken by both together = (x × y) ÷ (x + y). Total Work is treated as the LCM of the time taken.

Negative Efficiency (Outlet Pipe / Leakage)

An outlet pipe or a leakage empties the tank and is treated as doing negative work. Its efficiency must be subtracted from the inlet pipes to find the net efficiency.

Fractional Work Completion

The time required to complete a fraction of a task equals the required fractional work divided by the working efficiency, i.e., Fractional Time = (Total Time) × (Fractional Part).
</p

questions.question:
A shopkeeper offers the following four schemes.
A) Two successive discounts of 19% and 25%
B) Buy 7, get 6 free
C) Single discount of 50%
D) Two successive discounts of 3% and 39%

Which scheme is the best for the shopkeeper?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The best scheme for a shopkeeper is the one that gives the minimum discount percentage.

A: Effective discount = 19 + 25 − (19 × 25) ÷ 100 = 39.25%

B: Discount % = (6 ÷ 13) × 100 ≈ 46.15%

C: Discount % = 50.00%

D: Effective discount = 3 + 39 − (3 × 39) ÷ 100 = 40.83%

**∴ The correct answer is Scheme A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Scheme A = Two successive discounts of 19% and 25%

⇒ Scheme B = Buy 7, get 6 free

⇒ Scheme C = Single discount of 50%

⇒ Scheme D = Two successive discounts of 3% and 39%

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Effective Discount for x% and y% = (x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100)%

⇒ Buy X get Y free Discount % = (Y ÷ (X + Y)) × 100

 A
 
 39.25% (Min Discount)

 B
 
 46.15%

 C
 
 50.00%

 D
 
 40.83%

 
• 
 Discount % Comparison

**Calculations:**

⇒ To maximize profits, the shopkeeper needs to offer the scheme that gives the lowest discount.

⇒ Discount in Scheme A = 19 + 25 − (19 × 25) ÷ 100 = 44 − 4.75 = 39.25%

⇒ In Scheme B: Total items = 7 (paid) + 6 (free) = 13 items

⇒ Discount in Scheme B = (6 ÷ 13) × 100 = 600 ÷ 13 ≈ 46.15%

⇒ Discount in Scheme C = 50.00%

⇒ Discount in Scheme D = 3 + 39 − (3 × 39) ÷ 100 = 42 − 1.17 = 40.83%

⇒ Comparing all the discount percentages: 39.25% [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount

When two or more discounts are allowed one after the other on the marked price. The effective single discount of x% and y% is calculated using the formula: (x + y − xy ÷ 100)%.

Buy X Get Y Free

In this scheme, the total items received by the customer are (X + Y), while they only pay for X items. The discount percentage is calculated as: [Free Items ÷ Total Items] × 100.

Best Scheme for Customer vs Shopkeeper

The best scheme for a customer is the one providing the maximum discount value. Conversely, the best scheme for a shopkeeper is the one providing the minimum discount, allowing for maximum profit retention.
</p

questions.question: In the first round of elections, Amit received 63% of the votes. In the second round, his support decreased by 24%. What percentage of the total votes did Amit receive after the second round?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial votes Amit received = 63%.

His support decreased by 24%, meaning he retained (100% − 24%) = 76% of his initial voters.

New percentage of total votes = 63% × 76%.

⇒ 63 × 0.76 = 47.88%.

**∴ The correct answer is 47.88%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Initial Support = 63%

 
 
 Remaining Support
 (100% − 24%) = 76%

 
 
 Decreased
 by 24%

 
 Final Votes = 63% × 0.76 = 47.88%

**Given:**

Initial votes Amit received = 63% of total votes

Decrease in support in the second round = 24%

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (100% − Decrease%)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Decrease in votes = 24% of 63%

⇒ Remaining percentage of original votes = 100% − 24% = 76%

⇒ Final support Amit received = 76% of 63%

⇒ Final support = (76 ÷ 100) × 63%

⇒ Final support = 0.76 × 63%

⇒ Final support = 47.88%

**∴ The correct answer is 47.88%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Points vs Percentage Decrease

If a share drops from 63% to 39%, it is a drop of 24 *percentage points*. However, a *percentage decrease* of 24% means calculating 24% of the original 63%, acting as a relative reduction.

Multiplying Factor for Decrease

When a value decreases by R%, the new value is found directly by multiplying the original value by the factor (1 − R/100). Here, a 24% decrease gives a multiplying factor of 0.76.

Successive Percentage Changes

When calculating percentage of a percentage, we use the formula: Base Value × (1 ± A/100) × (1 ± B/100). Identifying the correct base is critical for solving percentage questions accurately.
</p

questions.question: A man buys a sofa set for ₹24,000. He spends ₹3,000 on repairs and sells it for ₹30,000. He again buys it back for ₹28,000 and sells at a loss of ₹1,200. What is the overall profit?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net profit is the algebraic sum of the profit and loss in all independent transactions.

Profit from 1st sale = ₹30,000 − (₹24,000 + ₹3,000) = ₹3,000

Loss from 2ⁿd sale = ₹1,200

Overall profit = ₹3,000 − ₹1,200 = ₹1,800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost price of the sofa (CP) = ₹24,000

Amount spent on repairs = ₹3,000

First selling price (SP₁) = ₹30,000

Second cost price (CP₂) = ₹28,000

questions.question: A 6-digit number 648XYZ is divisible by 4, 9 and 10. Find the value of X + Z – Y , where Y is the smallest possible number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divisible by 10 ⇒ Last digit Z = 0.

Divisible by 4 ⇒ Last two digits (Y0) must be divisible by 4. The smallest possible digit for Y is 0.

Divisible by 9 ⇒ Sum of digits (6 + 4 + 8 + X + 0 + 0) = 18 + X must be divisible by 9. So, X can be 0 or 9.

We need the value of X + Z − Y. For X = 0, the value is 0 + 0 − 0 = 0 (which matches the options).

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number = 648XYZ

Divisible by 4, 9 and 10

**Formula used:**

Divisible by 10 ⇒ Last digit = 0

Divisible by 4 ⇒ Last two digits divisible by 4

Divisible by 9 ⇒ Sum of digits divisible by 9

**Calculations:**

Divisible by 10 ⇒ Z = 0

Number becomes = 648XY0

Divisible by 4 ⇒ last two digits = Y0 divisible by 4

Possible Y = 0, 2, 4, 6, 8

Given Y smallest ⇒ Y = 0

Now number = 648X00

Divisible by 9 ⇒ sum of digits divisible by 9

Sum = 6 + 4 + 8 + X + 0 + 0 = 18 + X

⇒ 18 + X divisible by 9

⇒ X = 0 or 9

X is digit ⇒ X = 0

Now X = 0, Y = 0, Z = 0

⇒ X + Z − Y = 0 + 0 − 0 = 0

**∴ Final Answer = 0**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 4

A number is divisible by 4 if the number formed by its last two digits is perfectly divisible by 4 (e.g., 00, 04, 08, 12, etc.).

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is perfectly divisible by 9 if the sum of all its digits is a multiple of 9.

Divisibility Rule of 10

A number is perfectly divisible by 10 if and only if its unit digit is exactly 0.

questions.question: The points scored by a basketball team in a series of matches are as follows: 17, 2, 7, 27, 25, 5, 14, 18, 10, 24, 10, 8, 10, 12, 11. The value of the median is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the median, quickly arrange the 15 data points in ascending order.

Sorted Data: 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 10, 10, 11, 12, 14, 17, 18, 24, 25, 27

Since there are 15 terms (an odd number), the median is exactly the middle value.

The middle value is the 8th term in the sorted series.

Counting to the 8th term from either side gives 11.

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The points scored by a basketball team: 17, 2, 7, 27, 25, 5, 14, 18, 10, 24, 10, 8, 10, 12, 11

Total number of matches (n) = 15

**Formula Used:**

Median for an odd number of observations = [(n + 1) ÷ 2]th observation

 Data arranged in ascending order

**Calculation:**

⇒ Arranging the points in ascending order:

⇒ 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 10, 10, 11, 12, 14, 17, 18, 24, 25, 27

⇒ Number of observations (n) = 15 (which is odd)

⇒ Median = [(15 + 1) ÷ 2]th observation

⇒ Median = [16 ÷ 2]th observation

⇒ Median = 8th observation

⇒ Counting from the sorted data, the 8th observation is 11.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean

The arithmetic average of a dataset. It is calculated as the total sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations.

Mode

The value that appears most frequently in a given data set. A dataset may have one mode, more than one mode, or no mode at all.

Median for Even Number of Observations

If the number of terms 'n' is even, the median is the average of the (n ÷ 2)th term and the [(n ÷ 2) + 1]th term in the sorted list.

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship holds: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a cistern, individually, in 100 min and 25 min, respectively. There is a pipe located at the bottom of the cistern to empty it. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously, then the empty cistern gets filled in 40 min. How long will the pipe at the bottom of the tank take to empty the completely filled cistern if no other pipe is then open?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Total Work = LCM(100, 25, 40) = 200 units.

Combined filling efficiency = (200 ÷ 100) + (200 ÷ 25) = 2 + 8 = 10 units/min.

Net efficiency of all pipes working together = 200 ÷ 40 = 5 units/min.

Efficiency of the emptying pipe = 10 − 5 = 5 units/min.

Time taken by the emptying pipe alone = 200 ÷ 5 = 40 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A (filling) = 100 min

Time taken by Pipe B (filling) = 25 min

Time taken by all three pipes (A, B and empty Pipe C) = 40 min

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Time × Efficiency

**Calculation:**

Let Total Work be the LCM of given times.

⇒ Total Work = LCM(100, 25, 40) = 200 units

⇒ Efficiency of Pipe A + Efficiency of Pipe B − Efficiency of Pipe C = Overall Efficiency

⇒ 2 + 8 − Efficiency of Pipe C = 5

⇒ 10 − Efficiency of Pipe C = 5

⇒ Efficiency of Pipe C = 10 − 5 = 5 units/min

⇒ Time taken by Pipe C completely empty the cistern = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of Pipe C

⇒ Time taken = 200 ÷ 5 = 40 min

**∴ The correct answer is 40 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Trick

If two pipes fill a tank in x and y hours, and a third pipe empties it in z hours, the net part filled in 1 hour is (1/x) + (1/y) − (1/z).

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Time taken to complete a work is inversely proportional to efficiency. When work is constant, Time × Efficiency = Constant.

Work done by Emptying Pipe

An emptying pipe is always considered to have negative efficiency as it works against the filling pipes.

questions.question: The monthly incomes of two friends Ashish and Kiran, are in the ratio 5 : 8, respectively, and each of them saves ₹75,000 every month. If the ratio of their monthly expenditure is 2 : 4, find the monthly income of Ashish (in ₹).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Income ratio of Ashish to Kiran = 5 : 8 (Gap between parts = 3)

Expenditure ratio = 2 : 4 ⇒ 1 : 2 (Gap between parts = 1)

To equalize the horizontal gaps, multiply the expenditure ratio by 3 ⇒ 3 : 6

Now, Savings = Income − Expenditure = 5 − 3 = 2 units for both.

Since each saves ₹75,000, 2 units = ₹75,000 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹37,500.

Ashish's income = 5 units = 5 × 37,500 = ₹1,87,500.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,87,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of monthly incomes of Ashish and Kiran = 5 : 8

Ratio of monthly expenditures = 2 : 4 = 1 : 2

Savings of each person = ₹75,000

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

 Ashish (5 units Income)
 
 
 
 Exp: 3 units
 Save: 2 units

 Kiran (8 units Income)
 
 
 
 Exp: 6 units
 Save: 2 units

 2 units of Saving = ₹75,000

**Calculations:**

Let the monthly incomes of Ashish and Kiran be 5x and 8x respectively.

Expenditure of Ashish = 5x − 75000

Expenditure of Kiran = 8x − 75000

⇒ Ratio of expenditures = (5x − 75000) / (8x − 75000) = 1 / 2

⇒ 2 × (5x − 75000) = 1 × (8x − 75000)

⇒ 10x − 150000 = 8x − 75000

⇒ 10x − 8x = 150000 − 75000

⇒ 2x = 75000

⇒ x = 37500

⇒ Ashish's monthly income = 5x = 5 × 37500 = 187500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,87,500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

When two initial values in a ratio receive identical adjustments leading to a new ratio, cross-multiplying the ratios yields a quick algebraic setup to isolate the multiplier.

Income and Expenditure Relationship

Income = Expenditure + Savings. This fundamental linear equation is universally used to set up the corresponding variables in percentage and ratio-based salary questions.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The area of a regular n-sided polygon inscribed in a circle of radius R is (n / 2) × R² × sin(360° / n).

Ratio of areas = [6/2 × R² × sin(60°)] : [5/2 × R² × sin(72°)]

Ratio = (3 × √3 / 2) : (5/2 × √(10 + 2√5) / 4)

Ratio = (3√3 / 2) : (5√(10 + 2√5) / 8) = 12√3 : 5√(10 + 2√5)

**∴ The correct answer is 12√3 : 5√(10 + 2√5).**

questions.question: Successive discounts of 12% and 13% are equivalent to what single discount?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two successive discounts of A% and B%, the equivalent single discount is calculated using the formula:

Equivalent Discount = A + B − (A × B) ÷ 100

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 12 + 13 − (12 × 13) ÷ 100

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 25 − 156 ÷ 100

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 25 − 1.56 = 23.44%

**∴ The correct answer is 23.44%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First successive discount (D₁) = 12%

Second successive discount (D₂) = 13%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − D₁) ÷ 100 × (100 − D₂) ÷ 100

Equivalent Discount % = [(MP − SP) ÷ MP] × 100

**Calculations:**

Let the Marked Price (MP) be 100.

⇒ SP = 100 × (100 − 12) ÷ 100 × (100 − 13) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 100 × (88 ÷ 100) × (87 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 88 × 0.87

⇒ SP = 76.56

⇒ Equivalent Discount = MP − SP

⇒ Equivalent Discount = 100 − 76.56 = 23.44

⇒ Equivalent single discount percentage = 23.44%

**∴ The correct answer is 23.44%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount Formula

When two discounts x% and y% are given consecutively, the equivalent single discount is derived directly as [x + y − (x × y) ÷ 100]%.

Ratio Method for Multiple Discounts

Convert each percentage into a fraction. The product of original denominator values represents the total MP, and the product of reduced numerator values represents the final SP. Discount% = [(MP − SP) ÷ MP] × 100.

Buy X Get Y Free Offers

The equivalent discount percentage for such promotional offers is evaluated as: [Free items (Y) ÷ Total items (X + Y)] × 100.
